records.found: Nothing dated 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-09 reports a new placebo- or sham-controlled result for a drug that clears aged cells: no paper, no posted registry results, no company release. The stage record (registry number NCT04857996, the Unity eye trial) is unchanged since 2024-05-16. Flagged because the entry does not name a placebo-controlled trial now recruiting whose main measure is physical function (the TROFFi trial of fisetin in breast cancer survivors, registry number NCT05595499), and one website claims results for it that the registry does not support.

findings.what: The registry entry for the Mayo Clinic placebo-controlled trial of fisetin in people with Covid-19 (registry number NCT04476953, 80 people) was updated; it is still listed as active, not recruiting, with no results posted and completion estimated for March 2027.
The stage record, the Unity eye trial (registry number NCT04857996), shows completed, results posted 2024-05-16, last update 2024-05-16: no change in the window, and it agrees with the entry.

A design paper for the TROFFi trial was published in Therapeutic Advances in Medical Oncology: 88 postmenopausal breast cancer survivors, fisetin against placebo, main measure the change in six-minute walk distance. The registry entry (NCT05595499) was last updated 2026-07-17 and still says recruiting, with no results. The records do not name this trial.

A website (tetrapod.pages.dev) says TROFFi results showing a better walking distance were presented at a 2026 meeting. Not opened, no primary source found, and it conflicts with the registry status of recruiting; treat as unconfirmed.

records.found: On 2026-11-06 Nature Aging published a report (Wu and colleagues) that a mineral dietary supplement, vanadyl sulfate, given by mouth kills aged cells, eases several age-related conditions and extends lifespan in male mice. It is a further animal result on a rung the entry already holds; no human lifespan or healthy-years trial was published, registered or announced in the window, so the test for the next stage is not met.

findings.what: Nature Aging, "Altered protein cysteine reactivity in senescent cells is a vulnerability for senolysis to ameliorate aging" (Wu and colleagues): the abstract says the supplement by mouth "extends lifespan in male mice" and eases age-related disorders. Peer-reviewed; mice only, one sex named. The abstract was read at Europe PMC and the date confirmed at Crossref; the journal page asks for a sign-in, so the size of the lifespan gain was not read.

Cell, "Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis" (Kuehnemann and colleagues): a fatty acid given by mouth lowered markers of aged cells in old mice and improved age-related function. No lifespan result is stated in the abstract.

records.found: On 2026-11-05 a completed trial was first posted on the registry (registry number NCT07918261, Steadman Philippon Research Institute): 82 people over 55 given fisetin on one of two schedules, main measure the change in aged cells in the blood at 45 days; no results are posted and there was no placebo group. Its report exists only as a preprint of 2026-07-22, not peer-reviewed, which says markers of aged cells in blood cells fell from the start on both schedules. It does not change the stage, and no approval or routine clinical use was found. Also flagged: a peer-reviewed mouse report of 2026-03-17 (PNAS) that the two-drug course the entry rests on damaged nerve insulation in the brain is not in the records.

findings.what: Registry entry NCT07918261, "Evaluation of Fisetin to Reduce Systemic Senescence" (Steadman Philippon Research Institute), first posted 2026-11-05: phases 1 and 2, randomised between two dosing schedules, no placebo, 82 enrolled, run 2023-05-24 to 2024-01-30, status completed, main measure the change from the start in aged blood cells at 45 days. No results posted.

Preprint (Preprints.org, not peer-reviewed), Gao and colleagues, "Effects of Two Fisetin Dosing Regimens on Reducing Senescence-Related Genes in Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells in Aged Humans": 81 people, two schedules, no placebo; at day 45 both schedules lowered two gene markers of aged cells in blood cells compared with the start. This appears to be the report of the trial above. Abstract read at Europe PMC and Crossref; the preprint site refused the page.

PNAS, Lombardo and colleagues, "Senolytic treatment induces oligodendrocyte dysfunction and demyelination in the corpus callosum": young and old mice given dasatinib and quercetin developed significant loss of nerve insulation in the brain compared with untreated mice. A peer-reviewed safety finding in animals, against, on the same two drugs as the 2019 kidney report and the 2026 liver trial; the records do not hold it.

Trade coverage says a first trial in people of a skin cream from Rubedo Life Sciences (RLS-1496) reported fewer aged cells in skin in April 2026. Seen only in a search summary; not opened or checked. The registry lists a trial of the cream in sun-damaged skin (NCT07340697), last updated 2026-08-12.

Registry entry NCT07275359 (Duke University, a small uncontrolled study of metformin in older people with lung disease, with blood markers of ageing) was updated; not yet recruiting, start estimated February 2027.

records.found: On 2026-11-02 the company Immorta Bio announced by press release that a first person had been given its immunotherapy meant to make the immune system clear aged cells (SenoMune-0257), on 2026-10-29 in Mexico, in an investigator-run study of people with advanced cancer. It does not meet the test: the product is not engineered immune cells, no measurement of aged cells was reported, there is no peer-reviewed report, and no registry entry was found for it. No trial of engineered T cells against aged cells was registered or updated in the window.

findings.what: PR Newswire release, Miami, 2026-11-02, "First Human Administration of Senolytic Immunotherapy to Fight Cellular Aging Announced by Immorta Bio": "The first patient was treated on October 29, 2026, in Mexico", in "an independently conducted, investigator-initiated clinical study involving patients with advanced cancer"; the company supplied the product. No results, no registry number and no regulator are named, and the release says safety and efficacy in people have not been established.
Registry searches for the company and product names (SenoVax, SenoMune, Immorta) and for engineered immune cells against the uPAR protein returned no entry at all, in or out of the window.

unmatched.what: European Heart Journal Open published a double-blind randomised trial (61 people, 43 finished) of a multi-ingredient nutritional powder aimed at ageing mechanisms: after six months, artery function and stiffness and systolic blood pressure were better than on the control (registry number NCT06145087).
unmatched.why_it_matters: A controlled human trial of a product sold against ageing, with a pre-stated main measure met; small, with a high drop-out, and on a marker, not on disease or lifespan.

unmatched.what: The Journal of Clinical Investigation published a report that aged cells drive a form of muscular dystrophy in patient tissue and mice, and that an existing antiviral drug (lamivudine) reduced them in mice; the authors call for a trial.
unmatched.why_it_matters: Points to a possible first disease trial for a different way of quieting aged cells; animal work only.

unmatched.what: BioAge Labs issued its third-quarter 2026 results release; a search summary says first results of its trial in diabetic eye swelling are expected in the last quarter of 2026. Not opened.
unmatched.why_it_matters: An ageing-biology company with a human readout due within weeks; not a drug that clears aged cells, so it fits none of these five records.
